adjudication.rationale: In the new `remove_member` action, the diff changes removal to `group.users.delete(user_id)`. In Rails, `association.delete(id)` typically issues a direct delete on the join table (often via `DELETE ... WHERE ...` / `delete_all`) and does not invoke model-level callbacks on the join model nor any custom `Group#remove(user)` logic. The pre-diff code removed members via `group.remove(user)`, suggesting there is intended domain logic for removals. If `groups.user_count` is maintained via callbacks/counter-cache on the join model (consistent with the presence of `user_count` being used throughout the UI/serializers), this change can leave `user_count` stale after removals, while `add_members` still uses `group.add(user)` (which would run that logic). This is a concrete behavior change introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — `offset = params[:offset].to_i` is never clamped to >= 0 (the clamp lives only in JS), so `?offset=-1` reaches PostgreSQL as a negative OFFSET and 500s [conf=75, P2]

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — `group.users.delete(user_id)` for a non-member (double-click / stale list) resolves the id through the association and raises RecordNotFound instead of the previously-tested silent success [conf=75, P1]

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — offset is clamped against the stale pre-request user_count, so deleting the last member on the final page refetches at offset == total and renders an empty page labelled "N/N" [conf=75, P2]

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group.findMembers` the request offset is computed as `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))` before the AJAX call. After `removeMember`, it immediately calls `self.findMembers()` without first updating `user_count`/`offset`. If you delete the last member on the last page, the client still has the old (higher) `user_count`, so the clamped offset can remain at the old last-page offset (e.g. 100) even though the new total is smaller (e.g. 100 with limit 50 means valid last offset should be 50). That produces a fetch at `offset == total` (or beyond the new last page), which returns an empty `members` list and leaves the UI on an empty "N/N" page until the user navigates manually.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — `group.users.delete(user_id)` resolves to `delete_all` on the join table, bypassing GroupUser callbacks and the `counter_cache: "user_count"` decrement, so `groups.user_count` permanently over-counts with no repair migration or backfill [conf=75, P1]

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `remove_member` in `Admin::GroupsController` which removes a user via `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then calls `group.save`. For a `has_many :users` association (typically `has_many :users, through: :group_users`), `delete` removes join rows using `DELETE` SQL (often `delete_all`) and does not instantiate/destroy the join model, so join-model callbacks (and any `counter_cache` maintained via those callbacks) are skipped. This is a behavioral change from the removed code path that used `group.remove(user)` (likely destroying the join record). Since the app relies on `groups.user_count` (JS uses `user_count`, serializers return it), skipping the counter update can leave `user_count` stale/overcounted after removals.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:92 — `if group.save ... else render_json_error(group)` runs after the delete already committed, so a save failure reports 422 to a client whose membership row is already gone and the JS `.then()` never fires [conf=100, P3]

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code performs `group.users.delete(user_id)` before checking `if group.save`. The association deletion is executed immediately (and is not wrapped in a transaction with the subsequent `group.save`), so if `group.save` returns false and the controller responds with `render_json_error(group)` (422), the membership row has already been removed in the DB while the client sees a failure. On the client side, `Discourse.Group#removeMember` uses `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)`; a 422 would prevent the `.then` handler from running, so the UI may not refresh even though the member was actually removed. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` overwrites the column from a flat param in the same commit that changed the client payload shape, so a browser with cached pre-deploy JS during the rolling deploy window silently flips the group invisible and gets success_json [conf=75, P2]

adjudication.rationale: Yes. This diff changes the server to read `visible` from a top-level param (`group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` in `create` and `update`) while the previous API shape (shown removed in this diff) used nested `params[:group][:visible]`. If a client still sends the old payload during a rolling deploy (cached pre-deploy JS calling the old endpoints with `{ group: { visible: ... } }`), then `params[:visible]` will be nil and the code will set `group.visible` to `false` (`nil == "true"`), potentially flipping visibility silently while still returning success on save.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34 — `update` no longer reads `usernames` at all, so existing clients that sync membership via PUT /admin/groups/:id get 200 success_json with the entire membership payload silently discarded, with no deprecation shim or dual-write window [conf=100, P2]

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#update` was changed from reading `payload = params[:group]` and applying `group.usernames = payload[:usernames]` (for non-automatic groups) to only handling top-level `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, and `params[:name]` (with a guard for automatic groups). There is no longer any code path that reads or applies a `usernames` parameter in `update`, and the controller still returns `success_json` on save. Therefore a client that previously updated group membership by PUTing usernames to `/admin/groups/:id` would now get a 200 response while membership changes are ignored (membership changes were moved to new `add_members`/`remove_member` endpoints).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — pagination now applies to all groups while the public template only renamed its each-binding, so the public members page silently truncates at 50 with no way to reach the rest [conf=100, P2]

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In GroupsController#members the diff removes the old behavior that only applied limit/offset to automatic groups and now always applies pagination with a default `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, so callers that don’t pass `limit` will only ever receive 50 members. On the public side, `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` was changed to set the route model to the group and call `model.findMembers()`, and `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` only changes the iteration from `model` to `members`; there are no added pagination controls/actions in the public members template/route to advance `offset` (unlike the new admin controller which adds next/previous actions). As a result, the public members page will display only the first 50 members with no evident way to navigate to the rest.
